key_insight: Rare-earth silicate environmental barrier coatings are promising because they balance CMAS and water-vapor resistance, thermal expansion compatibility, and high-temperature stability, but performance depends strongly on composition, phase, and coating microstructure.
engineering_relevance: For CMC components in extreme heat, these coatings offer a path to longer service life, but only if phase selection and spray-induced defects are managed together.
method: Clarify phase-formation rules using thermodynamic and crystallographic reasoning
Compare single-component and multicomponent silicates in both bulk and coating forms
Summarize corrosion mechanisms and multi-objective design strategies under CMAS and water vapor
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates the review synthesizes composition-structure-property relationships and contrasts bulk ceramics with plasma-sprayed coatings, rather than presenting new experimental datasets.
watch_item: Bulk-material performance may not transfer directly to plasma-sprayed coatings because SiO2 loss, amorphous phases, porosity, and segregation can change corrosion behavior.
paper_title: Advances in Rare‐Earth Silicate Environmental Barrier Coatings
